The five trails

Cheshire Rail Trail

  • 43 mi
  • Bellows Falls to Winchendon

Rebuilt from Westmoreland through Keene to Troy. The Walpole end is not yet planned, and stretches near Fitzwilliam are in progress.

Parking: sample content needed from the board.

Ashuelot Rail Trail

  • 21.75 mi
  • Keene to Hinsdale

Rebuilt near Keene and Swanzey. Winchester and Hinsdale stretches are in progress or unplanned.

Peterborough to Hillsborough

  • 17 mi
  • Peterborough to Hillsborough

A rebuilt middle section, with the ends not yet planned.

Monadnock Rail Trail

  • 16 mi
  • Peterborough to Winchendon

Short rebuilt stretches near Jaffrey, with the rest in progress or not yet planned. A 4 mi connector links to Winchendon, MA.

Fort Hill Rail Trail

  • 8.5 mi

Work in progress. A bridge crosses the Connecticut River into Brattleboro.

About and donate

A volunteer-led nonprofit rebuilding the region's rail trails.

What we do

The Monadnock Region Rail Trail Collaborative brings together towns, nonprofits, snowmobile clubs and volunteers. We rehabilitate and maintain the Cheshire, Ashuelot, Fort Hill, Hillsborough and Monadnock rail trails.

The goal is a connected network linking southwest New Hampshire to Bellows Falls and Brattleboro, VT, and Winchendon, MA.

Who's on the board

  • Cheshire County
  • Keene
  • Keene Sno-riders
  • Jaffrey
  • Monadnock Conservancy
  • Southwest Region Planning Commission
  • Swanzey
  • Walpole
  • Winchester

How projects get funded

Federal grants usually cover about 70% of a project. Towns, volunteers, donors and local businesses cover about 30%.

Donate

Your gift helps cover the local match on grants for trail rebuilding, bridges and maintenance.

Plan my visit

Long rides on trail that's ready, with what to watch for.

Distances come from the status map and are approximate. Notes marked Heads up and Good to know are sample entries until the board confirms them.

Rebuilt   In progress

Westmoreland to Keene

  • About 12 mi one way
  • 24 mi round trip
  • Rebuilt the whole way
WestmorelandKeene
  • Good to know
    The whole route is rebuilt trail. Start from either end. Parking details coming soon.
  • Heads up
    Downed trees were reported near Westmoreland after storms. Check conditions before you go.
  • Not yet planned
    The trail north from Westmoreland toward Walpole has no work scheduled yet.

Keene to Troy, and beyond

  • About 12 mi one way
  • 24 mi round trip
  • First 2 mi still in progress
KeeneTroyFitzwilliam
  • Good to know
    Troy's restored depot is a natural stop, about 7 mi from Keene. Past Troy, rebuilt trail continues about 6 more miles.
  • Heads up
    A short stretch just southeast of Keene is still being finished. Expect rough ground or a detour.
  • Coming soon
    Work is under way on the last 3 or so miles into Fitzwilliam. This ride will get longer.

Westmoreland to Troy: the big day

  • About 19 mi one way
  • 38 mi round trip
  • About 2 mi in progress
WestmorelandKeeneTroy
  • Good to know
    Ride one way and arrange a pickup, or turn around at Keene for a 24 mi round trip. Keene makes a good halfway stop.
  • Heads up
    Covers the in-progress stretch southeast of Keene, plus the downed trees reported near Westmoreland.
  • Coming soon
    The route will extend toward Fitzwilliam once work under way south of Troy is finished.

Shorter rides

Keene to Swanzey on the Ashuelot is about 5 miles of rebuilt trail. Around Peterborough, about 6 miles are rebuilt.

Restoring the old rail corridors of the Monadnock region

Mile by mile, bridge by bridge, for every generation to use.

Find a trail

Five trails, one connected network

More than 100 miles of rail corridor run through southwest New Hampshire and reach into Vermont and Massachusetts. The map shows how far along each stretch is today.

  • Cheshire43 mi
    Bellows Falls, VT to Winchendon, MA
  • Ashuelot21.75 mi
    Keene to Hinsdale
  • Peterborough to Hillsborough17 mi
    Monadnock region, north
  • Monadnock16 mi
    Peterborough south to Winchendon, plus a 4 mi connector
  • Fort Hill8.5 mi
    Hinsdale to Brattleboro, VT

Rebuilt and ready   Work under way   Not yet planned

Mileage between towns is approximate.

The railroads that built the region

By the 1870s, rail lines tied Keene, Troy, Winchester and a dozen other towns to Boston and beyond. Depots, granite cuts and stone arch bridges are still standing. Our work gives those corridors a second life for walkers, riders, skiers and snowmobilers.

Who we are

Troy depot. Photo: Stuart Green / Trailspotting.com

Help finish the network

Grants cover about 70% of each project. Donations and volunteers help cover the rest.
